title: Endometriosis in pregnancy - effect on the risk of pregnancy and birth complications
summary: The observational study will investigate whether pregnant women with endometriosis have a different risk of certain pregnancy complications than pregnant women without endometriosis. For this purpose, a group of pregnant women with endometriosis will be recruited during pregnancy, observed during pregnancy and birth and compared with a healthy control group. In addition, a questionnaire will be used to ascertain whether pregnant women with endometriosis have an unmet need for counselling during their pregnancy. Births by caesarean section are followed up for up to five years with regard to the possible development of endometriosis at the caesarean scar. There is no intervention.
conditions: Disorders related to short gestation and low birth weight, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Pregnant women with endometriosis are monitored for pregnancy complications and asked to complete a questionnaire before delivery about their history and counselling needs during pregnancy.
Pregnant women without endometriosis are observed for pregnancy complications.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy; birth at the Charité Campi Mitte,
Virchow Klinikum or DRK Westend; ability to contract, existence of a declaration of consent; for case patients: anamnestically reported and documented endometriosis.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant women with severe maternal diseases; multiple pregnancies; abnormalities in the extended basic screening; uterine malformations.
basic screening; uterine malformations; previous operations on the uterus with
opening of the cavity; inability to give consent, lack of informed consent.
